Triage (daily round, session `session_01Kktexqp6uVuFMztvvTMf3V`, 2026-08-24): lands in `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-path.tsx` → `domain:ui` + `pm:queue`, Bug (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 — travelled/upcoming/lost state conveyed by colour alone; the glyphs are aria-hidden). Fix shape: give each stage a programmatic state (visually-hidden text or `aria-label`), keep the glyphs decorative.

## ⚠️ PREMISE CHECK FIRST — this file changed a few hours ago

**`record-path.tsx` was rewritten by PR #5917 (`fix(plugin-detail): render record:path as a readout, not a fake segmented control`, merged 2026-08-24), which closed a different card (#5768).** This card was filed *from inside* that work and says so: *"the readout markup was reworked in `claude/issue-5768-inert-lifecycle-path`, which de-buttoned the path but deliberately did not move its accessible semantics."*

⛔ **Do not take the card's JSX snippet as current source.** Re-read the landed file first and establish, against the shipped markup, whether the defect still stands: are the ✓/✗ glyphs still `aria-hidden`, and is `aria-current="step"` still the only programmatic signal? `premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is a **legitimate and valuable delivery** here — report it rather than manufacturing a diff.

## If the premise holds

The requirement is that a stage's **state** (travelled / upcoming / lost terminal) reaches the **accessible name**, not just colour and an `aria-hidden` glyph — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1. The card names two shapes (visually-hidden per-stage text, or an `aria-label` composing label + state); pick one and say why.

- **User-facing strings mean i18n keys** — ⛔ not the hardcoded English the component currently uses for its container labels. That is explicitly why this is its own card and not a one-liner.
- Verify with the **accessible tree**, not the DOM: the deliverable is that the stage's announced name carries its state. A test asserting a `class` or a `span` is not evidence about the accessible name.
- ⛔ **#5569** (approval-stepper duplication) is a **different surface with its own markup** — do not touch it or fold it in.

## ACCEPT — PR #5958, pending CI convergence

Reviewed against GitHub, not against the report's self-account. Landing waits on the gate read (PR opened 04:37:07Z; window ~04:46–04:48Z).

### Checklist

| item | reading |
|---|---|
| PR form | draft ✓, base `main` ✓, `Fixes #5916` ✓ |
| Premise re-check | **done against the shipped file**, not the card's snippet — see below |
| Scope vs. declared fence | 15 files / +506. Wider than it looks, and **justified** — verified independently below |
| Changeset | present, `patch` for `@object-ui/plugin-detail` + `@object-ui/i18n` |
| `#5569` | untouched, as fenced ✓ |
| CI | `unstable` — still converging, **not yet read** |

### The premise check was the point of this dispatch, and it was done properly

I briefed this card with an explicit falsification licence because `record-path.tsx` had been rewritten hours earlier by PR #5917. The dev re-read the **landed** file at `0b12a3315` and pinned each claim to a line: `✓` `aria-hidden` at `:177`, `✗` at `:175`, `aria-current="step"` at `:170`. Premise holds unchanged.

It also caught the thing most likely to have produced a false "already fixed" reading: #5917 added `data-stage-state` / `data-stage-terminal`, which *look* like state now reaches assistive tech. They don't — **a `data-*` attribute is not in the accessibility tree**, and they are test instruments. The PR amends #5917's own header to say so, which stops the next reader making that mistake.

### The shape was chosen by measurement, and that measurement is the most valuable thing here

The card offered two shapes and picked neither. I briefed "verify against the accessible tree, not the DOM." The dev probed it on this tree with the suite's own harness **before writing the fix**:

- `role="listitem"` wrapping `span.sr-only` + label → accessible name **`''`**
- `role="listitem"` with `aria-label="草稿, completed"` → **`'草稿, completed'`**

`listitem` is name-from-author only. So the visually-hidden shape — the card's first suggestion — would have **satisfied a DOM assertion while delivering nothing to the accessibility tree**. That is precisely the failure this card exists to prevent, and it was avoided by measuring rather than by picking the more familiar shape.

### Test design worth copying

- **Non-circular by construction.** Selection is positional (index among `listitem`s); assertion is by computed accessible name. The header explains why: with the fix reverted every name is `''`, so a name-keyed query would report "no such stage" rather than "wrong name."
- **Two independent non-vacuity guards.** One asserts every stage *has* a name at all, so a later case can't compare `''` to `''`. The other renders `en`/`zh`/`de` and asserts the three names are **distinct** — if `t()` were bypassed, or every pack carried English, every other case would still pass and only this one fails.
- **The defect restated as a partition**: 2 completed + 1 current + 3 upcoming = 6 stages. No stage ambiguous, none missed.
- **State follows the record, not the position** — mounting on `draft` shows zero completed, proving the names are computed rather than baked into markup.
- **Both rows asserted.** Desktop and mobile are both in the DOM (no CSS breakpoint in this env), so a regression reaching one viewport only would otherwise pass.
- **The glyphs stay decorative** and that is tested — the fix adds a text equivalent rather than un-hiding the `✗`.
- The **two-file split** (provider vs provider-less) is justified by a real mechanism: `createI18n` registers itself as react-i18next's module-global default and survives `cleanup()`, so sharing a file would silently resolve against whichever locale mounted first. Precedent cited.

### Ablation separates signal from noise

Deleting the single `aria-label` line → **15 red / 12 green**, matching the direction predicted in both suite headers *before* running. Red: exactly the name-bearing cases. Green: group A (the #5768 readout contract), the "`✗` stays `aria-hidden`" case, and the whole pre-existing `inertReadout` suite — none of which ever depended on the name. Mutation confirmed on disk by grep (1 → 0), restore verified byte-identical with `diff -q`.

### Scope — checked, not accepted on assertion

15 files exceeds a naive reading of my fence, so I verified the justification rather than taking it: the repo has **exactly ten locale packs** (`ar, de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh`) and the PR touches all ten plus `DETAIL_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS`. With `all-locales-key-parity` failing in **both** directions and `defaults-maps-mirror-en-pack` failing a map row the pack lacks, five keys is fifty pack rows plus five map rows **or nothing**. That is mechanically forced, and it sits inside "the i18n keys the change needs" as briefed. No breach.

### Follow-ups filed — and one note for triage

**#5956** (hardcoded English container labels, one on a role-less `div` that names nothing) and **#5957** (an unreached `won` terminus still distinguished by hue alone) are both filed unassigned with honest reasoning for not folding them in. #5957 is the more important one: it is the **same WCAG 1.4.1 class as this card**, on the one distinction this card left behind, and it is reachable without authors opting in (the `WON_TOKENS` heuristic). Declining it was right — the fix needs new user-facing copy in ten packs and nothing in the tree pins the wording — but it should not sit long.

⚠️ **Label shapes across this round's three findings are inconsistent**: #5954 carries `finding` + `domain:ui`, #5953 carries `domain:ui` only, #5957 carries **no labels at all**. All three remain visible to a triage sweep (bare cards are case ①, half-labelled are case ③), so nothing is lost — but flagging it for first touch. ⛔ Not grading them here.
